title: An 8b 10GS/s 2-Channel Time-Interleaved Pipelined ADC with Concurrent Residue Transfer and Quantization, and Automatic Buffer Power Gating
problem: Achieving >5GS/s 8b ADC conversion with pipelined architecture requires parallel residue transfer and quantization to eliminate the residue amplifier bottleneck, while managing power efficiency.
motivation: High-speed wideband applications demand ADCs at 10GS/s sampling rates; existing pipelined ADCs are limited to 3GS/s due to serialized sampling-quantization-amplification operations and residue amplifier overhead.
method: In a pipelined ADC, each stage must amplify the leftover signal (residue) from the previous stage before it can be quantized (converted to digital)—this amplification step becomes the speed bottleneck at high conversion rates. This design makes residue transfer (passing the leftover signal between stages) and quantization happen concurrently (at the same time) by using differential sampling (measuring both a signal and its complement) and a source-follower inter-stage amplifier (a simple, linear, wideband, low-power circuit that replaces the traditional residue amplifier). The chip also uses automatic common-mode-regulated power-gating to shut off unused buffer circuits without adding extra switching overhead.
key_novelty: The core innovation is concurrent residue transfer and quantization, which eliminates the residue amplifier bottleneck using only a simple source-follower circuit for inter-stage gain.
contributions: 8b single-channel pipelined ADC at 5GS/s (fastest for this precision)
Automatic common-mode power-gating without switching overhead
Maintains low output swing and linearity vs. prior residue-amplifier schemes

metrics.speedup: 5x faster single-channel vs. prior pipelined (5GS/s vs 3GS/s)

baselines: Prior pipelined ADCs with residue amplifiers (3GS/s)
limitations: Paper focuses on mixed-signal design; system-level integration and thermal analysis not discussed.
primary_theme: High-speed pipelined ADC via residue transfer parallelization
